globalGapCandidates.problem: bootstrap-project.sh has no mode to upgrade or reconcile an already-registered project — it hard-guards on .factory/project-context.json existing and exits 3, forcing every product repo that falls behind the central standard to reconcile manually (as this report's own work required).
globalGapCandidates.japaEvidence: Japa was registered at standard 0.2.0 on 2026-07-16; central advanced to 0.3.0 then 0.4.0 on 2026-07-17. Running remote-init.sh/bootstrap-project.sh against Japa today would exit 3 immediately with no path forward other than manual file-by-file reconciliation.
globalGapCandidates.whyUniversal: Any product repository registered before a central standard bump will hit this exact wall; the fix is expressible with no Japa-specific facts.
globalGapCandidates.proposedCentralChange: Add a --mode upgrade (or --mode reconcile) that, for an already-registered project, only creates files/fields missing relative to the current template/schema version (same [[ -e ... ]] || cp pattern already used for individual files) and bumps standardVersion/qualityStandardVersion, without requiring a full re-bootstrap.
globalGapCandidates.compatibilityImpact: Additive only — new flag, no change to existing new/existing bootstrap behavior.
globalGapCandidates.testRequired: A CI test that registers a project at an older simulated standard version, then runs --mode upgrade and asserts verify-project-registration.sh passes afterward with no pre-existing Japa-specific files touched.

globalGapCandidates.problem: There is no version-drift detection tool. A registered product's standard-lock.json can silently fall behind the central VERSION file indefinitely with nothing surfacing the drift, since verify-project-registration.sh only checks internal cross-file consistency, not currency against the live central VERSION.
globalGapCandidates.japaEvidence: Japa sat at 0.2.0 for a full day while central moved to 0.3.0 then 0.4.0, discovered only because this onboarding prompt explicitly stated expectedMinimumCentralVersion: 0.4.0 and I happened to fetch and compare the central VERSION file.
globalGapCandidates.whyUniversal: Every registered product repository is subject to the same silent-drift risk; the fix requires no product-specific knowledge.
globalGapCandidates.proposedCentralChange: Have verify-project-registration.sh optionally fetch (or accept as a parameter) the central repository's current VERSION and warn/fail if the local standardVersion is behind it, distinct from its existing internal-consistency checks.
globalGapCandidates.compatibilityImpact: Should default to a warning, not a hard failure, so it does not break existing CI that doesn't expect network access during verification.
globalGapCandidates.testRequired: A test that pins a stale standardVersion locally and asserts the tool reports drift against a mocked/fixture 'current' VERSION.
